item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption examined whether NSW development approval processes contained corruption risks that were not being managed.
item.support:
the Commission decided to consider whether there are unmanaged corruption risks in NSW 
development approval processes.

item.text: It considered 187 submissions alongside its inquiries, complaints and research, covering councillor roles, conflicts of interest, council land, consultants, planning agreements and political donations.
item.support:
received a total of  
187 submissions from a wide range of individuals, agencies and organisations.

item.text: The Commission concluded that councillors’ different roles did not themselves create a corruption risk, but supported clearer reasons for decisions and greater transparency.
item.support:
The Commission has concluded that these different roles are not in themselves a corruption 
risk

item.text: Its 24 recommendations address decision reasons, conflicts of interest, voting records, appeals, land dealings, consultants, planning agreements and political donations.
item.support:
That individual local councils implement systems that record how councillors vote on 
development matters.

item.quote:
The Commission has concluded that these different roles are not in themselves a corruption 
risk, and that its further consideration of most of these options is not warranted.

The 
Commission is of the view that the absence of reasons does not necessarily suggest corrupt 
conduct, however, it considers that reasons should be given for all development decisions.
